replies.text:
Check of commonly-missed items:

- Automated abuse of a reachable endpoint: design has "After the first password login" (password login endpoint) — covered by listed threat 1 (credential stuffing).
- Staff/admin/moderator screens showing user-supplied content: design states no such screen (only "mobile banking app lets customers log in with Face ID") — not applicable.
- Privileged actions without a record (delete/refund/role change/money movement): design states no such action; accountability of sessions is already covered by listed threat 6.
- Personal/financial documents or pages cacheable by browsers/proxies/CDNs: design names only "plain app storage" on the device — not applicable (storage exposure covered by threats 2 and 4).
- Attacker-controlled text reaching logs, CSV/exports, emails, headers: no such field or export in the design — not applicable.
- Single-reviewer threat 1 (rooted/jailbroken rewrites local biometric decision): same mechanism as listed threat 3 — covered.
- Single-reviewer threat 2 (unlocked phone, no re-authentication): listed threat 3 already names "an opportunistic thief, repair shop, family member" using the stored token — covered.
- Single-reviewer threat 3 (any face/fingerprint enrolled on the device opens the banking session): real for "uses biometrics only to unlock the screen" and is a different path from patching/hooking the app — not covered.

{
  "schema": "threatline.threatmodel.v1",
  "issueKey": "EVAL-01",
  "sketch": {
    "components": ["mobile banking app", "Face ID / device biometric unlock", "plain app storage", "password login API", "token refresh endpoint"],
    "dataStores": ["plain app storage (refresh token)"],
    "externalServices": ["platform biometric API"],
    "trustBoundaries": ["customer device to bank backend", "OS biometric enrolment to app session"],
    "dataClasses": ["credentials", "pii"],
    "exposure": "public",
    "llmFeatures": false
  },
  "threats": [
    {
      "stride": "Spoofing",
      "title": "Any extra face or fingerprint enrolled on the phone opens the banking session",
      "scenario": "Biometrics are used only as a screen unlock and are never re-bound to the stored credential, so the app accepts whatever identity the OS has enrolled. A partner, child or coercive abuser who knows the device passcode adds their own face or fingerprint to the device, then opens the banking app: the unlock succeeds with no bypass tooling and the stored refresh token is replayed as the real customer. No app patching or rooting is needed and the bank sees an ordinary valid session.",
      "component": "Face ID unlock in mobile banking app",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "rating": { "attacker": "anyone", "effort": "low", "reach": "one", "harm": "takeover" },
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "the app stores the refresh token in plain app storage and uses biometrics only to unlock the screen" },
        { "quote": "The mobile banking app lets customers log in with Face ID." }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V2.2.5"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-287"],
      "plainLanguage": "Because the app just asks the phone 'is this an enrolled face?', anyone who adds their own face to the phone can open the victim's bank account.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Bind biometric unlock to the enrolled credential",
        "given": "a customer who has enrolled biometric login and has a refresh token on the device",
        "when": "the set of biometrics enrolled on the device changes, or a biometric other than the one present at enrolment is used",
        "then": "the app must invalidate the stored token and require a full password login before banking access, using a biometric-bound key that the OS invalidates on biometric enrolment changes"
      }
    }
  ]
}
